ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 rider-side cancellation fee under NS-4; no refund, no account flag. Optionally remind the rider via RydeHELP that no ETA-based free-cancellation rule exists under NS-8 (informational).
ruling.reasoning:
The dispute is a rider-side cancellation of an instant booking. The trace settles NS-0 (cancelled_by = rider) on F2, which routes the fee to NS-4, not to the driver-cancellation no-show provisions [F2][NS-0]. The trace likewise settles, with ✓, that the cancellation came more than 3 minutes after matching — 21:33:20 against a 21:30:00 acceptance, i.e. 3 min 20 s = 200 s [F2][NS-4]. Under NS-4 a rider cancellation made later than 3:00 after matching makes the $6.61 fee stand, and the fee on record is $6.61 [F5][NS-4]. The non-payment of a surge does not affect the cancellation fee [F6][NS-4].

The rider's case is built on NS-1/NS-2, but those clauses govern a cancellation by the driver on a passenger-no-show claim. The record shows the opposite: the driver never pressed "I'm Here" and the platform recorded no automatic arrival, and driver_arrived_at is null [F4][F3][NS-1]. NS-1's preconditions — arrival tap within 200 m of the pickup and a continuous wait of more than 3 minutes — are therefore not merely unmet, they are inapplicable: they set the conditions for charging a rider a no-show fee after a driver-side cancellation, and no such charge or claim exists here [F3][F4][NS-1]. NS-2 is the mirror of NS-1 and only bites where a driver cancelled claiming a no-show and the NS-1 elements fail; it does not reach a rider-side cancellation [F2][NS-2].

The rider's strongest admitted ground — that the driver was still far away — is not a ground Ryde recognises. The driver's closest approach was 2137 m and he never came within 200 m [F1][NS-4], but NS-4 makes the fee turn on the rider's own cancellation time, and Ryde publishes no ETA-based free-cancellation rule [F1][NS-4]. The driver's chat "About 5 min, traffic" [F8] and his post-trip statement that he was on his way [F10] are, as the rider argues, statements rather than system records, and the traffic record shows 50–59 km/h flowing conditions with no incident and fair weather [F11][F12][F13]; none of this is needed, because NS-4 requires no driver-delay element at all [F8][F11][NS-4]. The rider's complaint shows no overcharge item beyond the fee itself — the fee is a published $6.61 cancellation charge [F5][FARE-1]. No unmet arrival precondition converts that into a refundable item.

RD-6 cannot be applied. It requires that the case be established against the driver (a RD-2 refund or a recorded RD-1 breach) before the 90-day route-dispute profile can add an account flag [F15][RD-6]. Here there is no established breach — the charge is valid under NS-4 — so the driver's 1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days cannot by itself produce a flag, and profile facts may not decide the case [F15][RD-6]. NS-7 has no work to do because no refund is due [F2][NS-7].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages ("How long will you be?"; "About 5 min, traffic") and the driver's statement ("I was on my way when the rider cancelled") [F7][F8][F10]. Nothing in them is a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; this is an ordinary fare dispute [F7][F8][SAFE-1]. No safety escalation arises.

Evidence is sufficient: the timeline, GPS and fare records settle every element NS-4 needs — who cancelled, when, and the fee charged — and the chat is complete and fully timestamped [F2][F3][F5][F9][NS-4].

F10 is only a statement and is not relied on to prove arrival; the driver being en route and communicative [F8][F10] is all that NS-4 needs, since the charge is a rider-side cancellation fee [F2][NS-4].
The traffic band shows flowing conditions and no incident was recorded [F11][F12][F13], but NS-4 contains no ETA or congestion defence, so the cause of any delay does not void the fee [F2][NS-4].

RD-6 requires the case first be established against the driver; with the charge valid under NS-4 there is no breach, and the driver's 90-day upheld no-show dispute [F15] cannot alone support an account flag [F15][RD-6].

The driver's claim that delay is corroborated by traffic is not sustained: the band is free flow and no incident or weather cause appears [F8][F11][F12][F13]; it is nevertheless irrelevant, as NS-4 has no delay element [F2][NS-4].
